accepted.s: According to the latest comparative assessment, India ranks first globally in which one of the following commodities?
accepted.x: India ranks first globally in milk production. Wheat, fruits and eggs are listed among commodities in which India ranks second.
accepted.tq: Direct one-fact recall using closely related global-rank distractors.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Milk — First globally
2. Wheat — Second globally
3. Pulses — First globally
4. Vegetables — Second globally

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: India ranks first in milk and pulses, and second in wheat and vegetables. Hence, all four pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Statement verification across a global-rank comparison list.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India is reported to be the second-largest producer globally of which one of the following commodities?
accepted.x: India ranks second globally in fruits. It ranks first in pulses and spices, and second in silk as well, but the specified answer here is fruits.
accepted.tq: Direct recall with confusable first- and second-rank commodities.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding India's position in silk production is correct?
o: India produces only two commercial varieties of silk.
India produces all commercial silks except mulberry silk.
India ranks first globally in silk production and does not produce other natural fibres.
India is the only country producing all five commercial silks.
accepted.x: India is the only country that produces all five commercial silks.
accepted.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination using an exclusive production distinction.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's global position in fish production, as stated in the comparative assessment, is
accepted.x: India ranks third globally in fish production.
accepted.tq: Direct numerical recall with ascending rank options.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. India is the largest rice exporter and accounts for about 40% of global rice trade.
2. India also leads in dry onions.
3. India is the largest producer of rice according to the latest ministerial statement cited.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India leads in dry onions, is the largest rice exporter with about 40% of global trade, and was stated by the Union Agriculture Minister to be the world's largest rice producer, ahead of China.
accepted.tq: Statement combination involving a current-affairs distinction in rice rankings.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's rice production was reported as 150.18 million tonnes, compared with China's
accepted.x: India's reported rice production was 150.18 million tonnes, while China's was 145.28 million tonnes.
accepted.tq: Numerical comparison using close ascending values.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following commodities is correctly matched with India's reported global rank?
o: Rice — Second, according to the latest ministerial statement
accepted.x: India is the world's largest producer of pulses. The latest ministerial statement placed India first in rice, milk is first, and wheat is second.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched item among reversed global rankings.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's foodgrain production in 2024–25 was recorded at
accepted.x: Foodgrain production in 2024–25 was a record 357.73 million tonnes, equivalent to 3,577.3 lakh tonnes. The figure of 367.72 million tonnes refers to horticulture production.
accepted.tq: Numerical recall distinguishing foodgrain and horticulture figures.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following comparisons between foodgrain and horticulture production in 2024–25 is correct?
o: Horticulture exceeded foodgrains, with production of 367.72 million tonnes.
Horticulture production was below the 2018–19 foodgrain figure.
Foodgrains exceeded horticulture by about 10 million tonnes.
Both were recorded at approximately 357.73 million tonnes.
accepted.x: Horticulture production was 367.72 million tonnes, exceeding foodgrain production of 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Comparison-table based identification of the larger value.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The production of foodgrains in 2018–19, according to the third Advance Estimates, was approximately
accepted.x: Foodgrain production in 2018–19 was estimated at 283 million tonnes. The higher figures relate to 2024–25 production.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of an older benchmark figure with current-year distractors.
accepted.sec: India's global rank - crops, milk, fruits, silk, spices  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only commodities in which India ranks first globally?
accepted.x: India ranks first globally in milk, pulses and spices. Wheat, fruits, vegetables, eggs, cotton and silk are listed among commodities in which India ranks second.

accepted.s: Cereal yield is defined as the quantity of cereals produced per kilogram of
accepted.x: Cereal yield is measured in kilograms per hectare of harvested land under cereals.
accepted.tq: Precise-definition discrimination among similar agricultural-area terms.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as a major cause of India's cereal-yield gap?
o: Rainfed farming covering about 50–51% of net sown area
Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure
Small and marginal holdings forming about 86% of holdings
A skewed NPK ratio and low seed replacement rate
accepted.x: Universal access to efficient cold-chain infrastructure is not a stated cause; rather, cold-chain losses account for about 30%. The other three factors contribute to the yield gap.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by reversing a stated constraint into an advantage.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding climate-related yield effects:

1. Yields fall by about 8% for every 1°C rise in temperature.
2. Wheat yields may fall by 6–10% under heat stress.
3. A 1°C rise can wipe out about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements reflect the reported effects of heat on agricultural productivity: around 8% yield loss per 1°C, wheat losses of 6–10%, and the loss of about four years of rice and wheat productivity gains.
accepted.tq: Statement verification using related climate-impact figures.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: In El Niño years, the area under pulses generally falls by
accepted.x: Pulse area falls by about 2–9% in El Niño years. Yield or output declines are reported in separate ranges.
accepted.tq: Distinguishing area, yield and output percentage ranges.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following measures is most directly associated with improving seed quality through seed replacement and varietal replacement?
accepted.x: Better seed quality is promoted through the Seed Replacement Rate and Varietal Replacement Rate, abbreviated as SRR and VRR.
accepted.tq: Application of paired agricultural abbreviations to a stated pathway.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with its pathway for raising agricultural productivity?
o: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana — silk production
accepted.x: Custom Hiring Centres, or CHCs, promote mechanisation by making farm machinery available for hiring. Soil Health Cards promote balanced nutrition, while DSR is a crop-establishment practice.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure functional pair and eliminate swapped purposes.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana is intended to cover how many low-productivity districts during 2025–26 to 2030–31?
accepted.x: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana covers 100 low-productivity districts during 2025–26 to 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Direct numerical recall of scheme coverage and period.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following crops is identified as an exception to India's generally lower yields compared with global averages?
accepted.x: India's yields of cereals, maize, soybean and pulses trail global averages, whereas groundnut is identified as an exception because of semi-arid concentration and improved varieties.
accepted.tq: Exception-based recall from a comparative yield statement.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Rice — Approximately 67% irrigated
2. Pulses — Approximately 26% irrigated
3. Average operational holding size — 1.08 hectares
4. Soybean in many districts — Below 2 tonnes per hectare

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Rice is approximately 67% irrigated, pulses approximately 26% irrigated, the average holding size is 1.08 hectares, and soybean yields are below 2 tonnes per hectare in many districts.
accepted.tq: Statement verification combining irrigation, holding-size and yield figures.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of El Niño on pulses?
o: Acreage rises by 2–9% and output rises by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 2–9% and output falls by 6–30%.
Acreage falls by 6–30% and output falls by 2–9%.
Acreage remains unchanged while output rises by 5–25%.
accepted.x: In El Niño years, pulse acreage declines by about 2–9%, while output declines by about 6–30%.
accepted.tq: Separating two similar percentage ranges by the variable they describe.
accepted.sec: Yield concepts and gaps - cereal yield, causes, pathways  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following crops experienced a fall in area of 18 lakh hectares, with output declining to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025–26 from about 350 lakh bales?
accepted.x: Cotton area fell by 18 lakh hectares, and its output declined to 290.91 lakh bales in 2025–26 from approximately 350 lakh bales.
accepted.tq: Linking a crop with its distinctive area and output figures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a recent change in India's cotton trade position?
o: India became a net importer of silk owing to cotton-area expansion.
India became a net importer of raw cotton following declining output and area.
India discontinued raw-cotton imports because of higher cotton yields.
India became a net exporter of raw cotton after a rise in domestic output.
accepted.x: India became a net importer of raw cotton after declines in cotton area and output.
accepted.tq: Cause-effect recall with reversed trade-position distractors.

accepted.s: Between 2023 and 2024, soybean area in Madhya Pradesh declined by approximately
accepted.x: Soybean area in Madhya Pradesh fell by 10% between 2023 and 2024.
accepted.tq: Direct percentage recall using nearby crop-area figures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about crop-area trends in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Jowar and ragi expanded while groundnut remained unchanged.
Paddy and pulses continued to decline in 2024–25 after recovery.
Groundnut area rose from 3.46 to 11.36 lakh hectares.
Groundnut area fell from 11.36 to 3.46 lakh hectares, while jowar and ragi also shrank.
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, groundnut area declined from 11.36 to 3.46 lakh hectares, and jowar and ragi also shrank. Paddy and pulses recovered in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Long-statement trap using reversed area trends and figures.
accepted.sec: Area trends - stagnant or declining crops  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses, covering 2025–26 to 2030–31, has a financial outlay of
accepted.x: The Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses has an outlay of ₹11,440 crore.
accepted.tq: Direct scheme-outlay recall with ascending monetary options.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses:

1. It targets production of 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares.
2. It provides for 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor.
3. It covers the period 2025–26 to 2030–31.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The mission targets 350 lakh tonnes from 310 lakh hectares, provides 100% MSP procurement for tur, urad and masoor, and runs from 2025–26 to 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Statement combination covering targets, procurement and time period.
accepted.sec: Area trends - stagnant or declining crops  [other exams]

accepted.s: Total factor productivity in agriculture refers to
o: output growth not explained by growth in inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser
the total value of agricultural exports divided by farm employment
output growth explained only by expansion of cultivated land
the ratio of fertiliser use to cropped area
accepted.x: Total factor productivity is the part of output growth that cannot be explained by increased use of inputs such as land, labour, capital and fertiliser.
accepted.tq: Definition-based discrimination against single-input productivity measures.
accepted.sec: Total factor productivity - trend and drivers

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated driver of agricultural total factor productivity?
o: A mandatory reduction in all forms of farm mechanisation
accepted.x: Research, new varieties, irrigation, rural roads, markets, extension and education are stated drivers of agricultural TFP. A mandatory reduction in mechanisation is not a stated driver.
accepted.tq: Find the non-driver among a list of productivity-enhancing factors.
accepted.sec: Total factor productivity - trend and drivers

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about agricultural total factor productivity in the cited material is correct?
o: No estimate of India's agricultural TFP growth is provided; TFP is discussed for the whole economy.
Agricultural TFP growth is discussed only as a component of foodgrain production.
Agricultural TFP is defined as the increase in fertiliser consumption alone.
A precise estimate of India's agricultural TFP growth is provided.
accepted.x: The cited material does not provide estimates of India's agricultural TFP growth; it discusses TFP only for the whole economy.
accepted.tq: Scope discrimination between a defined concept and an unavailable estimate.
accepted.sec: Total factor productivity - trend and drivers
